score.doctor_final_text: I'm relieved to hear you might have an answer because this pain is so frustrating. What exactly do you think is causing these shocks every time I eat? Is this something related to my ear surgery or something else entirely?

dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help me understand what's going on, could you tell me when exactly this shooting ear pain first started following your tympanoplasty?
It started a few weeks after my surgery, but it only really happens when I'm chewing or eating something. It's a quick, sharp pain that comes and goes.
That is very helpful to know. Could you describe exactly what happens when you try to wear earrings, and have you noticed any swelling or redness around the earlobe or the surgical site?

It doesn’t look red or swollen, but my earrings just feel uncomfortable and irritating against my skin lately. I've actually stopped wearing them because the pressure seems to trigger that same dull ache.

I see. Have you noticed any clicking or popping in your jaw when you chew, or any numbness in the skin around your ear? 

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

Does the pain radiate to your temple or jaw when it happens, and have you noticed any skin color changes or sweating on that side of your face when you eat?

REQUEST TEST: Cranial_N
RESULTS: Gag reflex intact. Uvula is midline. Even and symmetric molar teeth bilaterally.
When you touch the area just in front of your ear or your temple, does it trigger that sharp shooting pain? I'd also like to check if you have any tenderness or unusual sensitivity when that area
Yes, it definitely feels tender right there in front of my ear when I press on it. It's not exactly the sharp shooting pain, but it feels very tight and sore, almost like a dull ache that lingers.

I understand. Did you have any issues with your jaw or ear sensitivity before the surgery, and where exactly does the earring cause the most discomfort—on the lobe or the cartilage near the ear canal?

REQUEST TEST: TMJ_Evaluation
RESULTS: No jaw clicking heard. No tenderness with palpation. Even and symmetric molar teeth bilaterally.

Could you tell me where exactly the surgical incision was located, and whether that sharp pain feels more like an electric shock or a burning sensation? I would also like to check the sensitivity of the skin in
The incision was behind my ear, but the pain feels more like a sudden electric shock that jumps through my jaw. It’s very sharp and quick, not really a burning feeling at all.

Does the sharp pain happen most intensely with the very first bite of a meal, and is the skin on your earlobe currently numb or overly sensitive to a light touch? I'd like to check the sensation around your ear and jaw.

REQUEST TEST: Sensory_Testing_Ear_Distribution

RESULTS: Right postauricular tapping causes tenderness in right tonsillar area. No tenderness with palpation of preauricular or mandibular areas. Normal gag reflex and midline uvula. Even and symmetric molar teeth.
Does the sharp pain ever happen when you swallow or cough, and have you noticed any change in your sense of taste lately? I’d like to see if we can pinpoint any other triggers for these
Now that you mention it, I do feel that sharp jolt when I swallow, though I haven't noticed any changes in how food tastes. It’s that same electric feeling that I get when I'm eating.
That is very specific. Have you noticed any sharp pain specifically in the back of your throat or at the base of your tongue when this happens, and does anything like cold liquids make it worse?

The pain is definitely deeper back toward the throat area when it hits, rather than just in my ear. I haven't noticed cold drinks making it worse, but swallowing anything solid or even just my own saliva can trigger that shock.
Given the location of your pain and the triggers you've described, I'm starting to form a clearer picture. Does the pain ever travel down into your neck, and have you felt
No, the pain doesn't really travel down into my neck; it stays concentrated around my ear and deep in my throat. It's just that sudden, sharp jolt that happens right when I swallow or chew.
When the sharp pain occurs, does it feel like there is a foreign object or a "lump" stuck in your throat? Also, does rotating your head or neck to one side trigger that electric shock

It doesn't really feel like a lump is stuck, just that sudden lightning bolt when I move my jaw or swallow. I have noticed that if I turn my head a certain way while eating, it seems to make that sharp jolt happen more easily.

How long do those electric shocks usually last when they occur, and are they strictly on one side of your throat and ear? I would also like to perform a specific palpation to check for any underlying structural
The shocks are very brief, only lasting a second or two before they vanish as quickly as they came. They are strictly on my right side, right where I had my ear surgery.
Since the pain is triggered by swallowing and turning your head, does it feel more intense when you swallow solids compared to liquids? I'd like to check for any structural issues in your neck area.

It definitely feels more intense when I swallow solids, probably because I have to chew and move my jaw more. Liquids still trigger that quick shock sometimes, but the heavier swallowing with food is much worse.

Does opening your mouth wide or yawning also trigger that sharp electric jolt? I would like to check for any structural issues near your skull base.

RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS

My voice hasn't changed at all, and I can speak just fine even when the pain hits. I haven't noticed any issues inside my mouth, it's just that sharp jolt triggered by the movement of swallowing or chewing.
